scope: Partitions all 18 canonical domains into migration waves. Wave numbers are the OUTPUT of a topological-level computation over audit/migration-dependency-graph.json's prerequisite edges (longest-path leveling: level(domain) = 1 + max(level(prerequisite)) for each prerequisite, 1 if none) — not chosen by hand. Every domain belongs to exactly one wave.
algorithm: Standard DAG longest-path leveling. Run once against the 32 prerequisite edges in audit/migration-dependency-graph.json; completed without a circular-dependency error (see that file's cycleCheck). Full computation reproduced below for auditability.

waves.name: Foundation
waves.rationale: Zero prerequisites — every other domain's canonical destination requires an identity.id to exist first. metadata's structural fields (schemaVersion, createdAt, lastUpdated) can be stamped the moment a record is created, alongside identity; its one exception (dataCompletenessScore) is handled separately — see 'metadata exception' below.

waves.name: Direct identity-dependent domains (parallel-safe)
waves.rationale: All 8 domains have exactly one hard prerequisite (identity) per audit/migration-dependency-graph.json — none depends on any other domain in this wave, so all 8 are topologically parallel-safe. Because the wave is large, a documented, measurement-based SUB-ORDERING is provided below to sequence the actual migration work within the wave — this sub-ordering is a prioritization aid, not an additional hard dependency.

subOrdering.method: Two measured criteria, applied in order: (1) x-provenance from schemas/name-entity.schema.json — computed fields (no possible missing-data state) before researched fields (can be legitimately incomplete); (2) within researched fields, audit/knowledge-roi.json's Knowledge Recovery Score, descending (Phase 1D) — the field whose migration resolves the most currently-rendered fallback/disclosed occurrences first.

order.reason: computed; also the domain with an exhaustively-confirmed 100% duplicate dataset (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json) — the single lowest-risk migration in the entire graph.
new domain, zero current data — trivial to introduce (nothing to migrate, only a new empty structure to activate).
researched; Knowledge Recovery Score 100 (audit/knowledge-roi.json) — highest measured leverage of any field on the site.

researched; migrates in the same data-build step as origin (scripts/apply-origin-enrichment.js merges both from one source in one pass) — grouped immediately after origin for that reason, not independently scored by Phase 1D.
researched; Knowledge Recovery Score 21, and the domain currently at 0% coverage sitewide (audit/knowledge-coverage.json) — lowest current data volume to migrate of the researched fields.

waves.name: Second-order dependents
waves.rationale: Each domain in this wave has at least one hard or soft prerequisite inside wave 2. usage (hard: popularity), relatedNames (hard: origin + classification + popularity), and relationships (hard: origin + classification + popularity + pronunciation) have genuine data dependencies verified against generator source. etymology/history/culture/religion have only a SOFT (conceptual, not data-driven) dependency on origin/language, because none currently has any data to migrate — see the per-domain note below.

waves.name: Terminal
waves.rationale: The unique domain whose entire purpose is to reference OTHER researched domains (meaning, origin, etymology, history) — by definition it cannot be migrated before what it cites exists. Correctly computed as the single highest topological level (4) in the graph.

metadataException.handling: Not wave-gated. This one field is defined to be recomputed continuously as every wave completes, since its value (fraction of non-null leaf fields) is only accurate once the current migration state of ALL other domains is known. It is placed in Wave 1 for validation purposes (every domain must belong to exactly one wave — audit/migration-validation.json), with this note as the documented exception, rather than inventing a fictitious 'Wave 5' for one sub-field of an otherwise-Wave-1 domain.

softDependencyDomains.note: Zero current data (audit/knowledge-domains.json) — there is nothing to migrate. The soft dependency is a recommendation for when real etymology research begins in a future phase, not a migration blocker.
